text:
jun: Ran nsys capture on the failing workload (long-prefill + mixed-batch). looks like a different hotpath popped after the kv-cache change. attaching top lines below.

perf-bot: nsys report ready: /artifacts/nsys/2300012345/trace.qdrep

jun: Top kernels by GPU time (nsys summary):
1) attention_forward_fp16_fused (34.1%)
2) kv_cache_prefetch (22.7%)
3) continuous_batch_coalesce (12.8%)
4) softmax_reduction (8.5%)
5) schedule_dispatch (5.9%)

anika: wait, kv_cache_prefetch at 22%? that's new vs last week's baseline where it was ~6%.

mike: hmm could be prefetch thrash after the 'lazy-evict' patch. did you run with KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=16?

jun: yes, env: KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=16, BATCH_COALESCE=auto, Q_ATTN_OPT=1. I also see increased SM stall reasons pointing to memory dependency during kv_cache_prefetch.

elaine: can you paste perfetto timeline excerpt? curious if prefetch is overlapping with dispatch.

jun: snippet from perfetto flame:
```
[0.000s - 0.220s] schedule_dispatch -> continuous_batch_coalesce -> kv_cache_prefetch
kv_cache_prefetch spans many small launches (avg 3.2ms) back-to-back, high L2 traffic
attention_forward_fp16_fused runs in between but with lower concurrency
```

anika: small launches + lots of L2 = kernel launch overhead + cache thrash. that will kill occupancy.

mike: NVPROF sample (sm_util): kv_cache_prefetch median SM% = 28, attention_forward_fp16_fused median SM% = 62, but kv_cache_prefetch has huge variance and many tiny kernel invocations.

jun: nvprof showed warp_serialize and memory_dependency as top stall reasons for prefetch kernels. i guess we're causing contention on global loads to the KV region.

anika: question: are prefetches using coalesced loads? maybe alignment/stride changed when we moved to packed indices.

jun: code excerpt:
```c++
// prefetch kernel launcher
for (int i = 0; i < N; i += PREF_STEP) {
  launch_prefetch_kernel(..., indices + i, PREF_STEP);
}
```
we switched from PREF_STEP=64 -> 16 recently.

elaine: that explains a lot. smaller steps -> more launches -> lower occupancy and L2 hotspot. revert to 64 for a test? or batch adjacent prefetches into one kernel.

mike: also check kernel selection: runtime picks a small-prefetch variant when sequence length < 128. that logic may mis-classify due to batching heuristic change.

jun: good catch. I see runtime logs: "selected kernel: prefetch_v_small" for many lanes where seq_len was 140 but effective_context trimmed to 120 due to padding trimming. off-by-1 bug in coalesce logic?

anika: sounds like two orthogonal issues: 1) PREF_STEP reduction causing launch storm 2) heuristic mis-selection when coalescer trims padding. both can push prefetch into a bad codepath.

jun: proposed short plan:
- revert PREF_STEP->64 locally and re-run nsys (jun)
- add guard to coalescer to avoid trimming below 128 for kernel selection (anika)
- add aggregated prefetch kernel that handles variable indices in a single launch (mike/elaine)

mike: I'll prototype aggregated prefetch this afternoon. should reduce launch count significantly.

elaine: I'll push a small runtime guard patch: if trimmed_context < 128 then force 'prefetch_v_default' selection. will open PR and tag jun/test.

jun: re-run after reverting PREF_STEP: results look promising. kv_cache_prefetch drops from 22.7% -> 7.1% and overall end-to-end p50 latency ~ -12%. attaching new nsys summary.

perf-bot: artifact uploaded: /artifacts/nsys/2300012345/run-after-prefetch-revert.qdrep

anika: excellent. let's keep aggregated prefetch as follow-up for next sprint. also add a small perf regression test to catch future PREF_STEP changes.

jun: noted. i'll write a microbench for kv prefetch pattern and add it to ci/perf-metrics.

mike: FYI, NVPROF flame shows softmax_reduction also got slightly noisier — might be due to earlier scheduling shifting concurrency. keep an eye but not blocking.

elaine: thanks all. created PR #1123 for selection guard and jira PERF-872 for aggregated-prefetch.

jun: closing loop — patch merged to canary, perf baseline stable. will monitor graphs tomorrow. :thumbsup:
